He replied, 'I had originally kept that shawl for you but when the two of you came together, it occurred to me that she was more closely related to Rasulullaah ﷺ than you are (I therefore gave preference to the relatives of Rasulullaah ﷺ over my own).'"[^1]
The Practice of Ameerul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Ali (RA)

Hadhrat Asbagh bin Nubaata reports that a man came to Hadhrat Ali (RA) saying, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! I have a need that I have already placed before Allaah before coming to you. If you are able to fulfil it, I shall praise Allaah and be thankful to you. If you are unable to fulfil it, I shall praise Allaah and excuse you." Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Write down your request on the ground because I do not like to see the humiliation of begging on your face." The man then wrote that he was a destitute. Hadhrat Ali (RA) instructed that a set of clothing be brought to him and when it came, he gave it to the man. The man wore the clothes and the recited the following couplets (in praise of Hadhrat Ali (RA), which mean):

"You have given me clothing, the beauty of which will soon fade
While I shall give you the most excellent clothing of praise
Should you receive my good praise, you have received great honour
And you will want nothing else in return for what I have to say
Praise revives the mention of a person
Just as the waters of the rain revive the plains and mountains
Never give up the good that Allaah inspires you to do
Because every servant shall be rewarded for the deeds they do"

Hadhrat Ali (RA) then sent for some gold coins and when a hundred coins were brought to him, he gave it all to the man. To this, Hadhrat Asbagh remarked, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! A set of clothing and a hundred gold coins?!" Hadhrat Ali (RA) replied, "Certainly! I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Treat people according to their status' and this is the status of this man in my regard."[^2]
The Reward of giving a Muslim Clothing to wear

When a beggar once came to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA), he asked the man, "Do you testify that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah and that Muhammad ﷺ is Allaah's Rasul?" When the man replied in the affirmative, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) asked him further, "And do you fast during Ramadhaan?" "Yes," was the reply.
